Drug Prevention Money Presented –

From State News Service
October 26, 1998

(SPRINGFIELD, IL) -- A new state survey shows that three out of ten 17-year-olds in Illinois have tried marijuana in the past month. Such statistics are prompting a new drug prevention program.
(Marijuananews note: As usual, the emphasis is on marijuana.)

Twenty-seven Illinois communities are getting state funds to fight drug use among young people. The governor’s office announced plans to spend two-and-a- half-Million-dollars on youth drug prevention grants. The money is designed to fund programs that focus on innovative prevention ideas... targeted at young people between the ages of 12 and 17.

(NOTE: The grant money is going to: Waukegan Township, University of Illinois Chicago Health Research & Policy Centers, Windows of Opportunity in Chicago, Project 18 in Urbana, Chestnut Health Systems, Plano Community Coalition for Wellness, Des Plaines Valley Community Center, Sinnissippi Centers in Dixon, McHenry County, regional office of Education 46, Rez Addiction Counseling Center in Elgin, Princeton Township High School, Save Our Neighborhood in Chicago, Tazewell County, Breaking Free in Naperville, Lake County, Belleville Area college, Youth Service Project in Chicago, Albany Park Community Center in Chicago, Ben Gordon Center in Wood Dale, Stephenson County, Partners in Education, Pledge for Life in Kankakee, Community Health and Emergency Services in Cairo... and Central East Alcoholism and Drug Council in Mattoon.)
